summary: Proposes an IANA registration extending the SIP Reason header for use in a BYE request when a session is preempted, either at a user agent or in the network by a reservation protocol such as RSVP or NSIS. It tells the terminated user agent what happened. It is standards-track.

eli5.summary: When a call is cut off to make room for a more important one, this adds a note to the hangup message explaining why.

subtitle: A new SIP Reason value that tells a hung-up party the call was cut off to make room for a higher-priority one.

tldr.problem: When a SIP session is torn down because a more important session needs the resources, the other party gets a BYE with no good way to say why. Existing SIP status codes and Q.850 causes do not fit an established session that was purposely preempted.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4411 registers a new Reason header protocol value, Preemption, with four cause codes that say whether the preemption happened at a user agent, in the network, was generalized for the last hop, or happened in a non-IP network.
tldr.outcome: The terminated user agent and SIP servers on the path can tell which kind of preemption occurred. The RFC also creates a new IANA registry of default reason-text strings.

today: RFC 4411 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 3326 and works alongside RFC 4412.

sections.title: Why Preemption Needs a Reason
sections.content:
With the SIP Resource-Priority (R-P) header from RFC 4412, sessions can be torn down because there are not enough resources for them to continue. Some domains will let a more important session replace a less important one, either at a user agent (UA) or at a congested router interface. Which sessions count as more important is out of scope for the RFC.

The SIP Reason header (RFC 3326) is meant to be carried in a BYE request to explain why a session ended. Q.850 has cause 8 for preemption and cause 9 for preemption with a circuit reserved for reuse, but cause 9 does not apply to IP, which has no circuits. The RFC says no other means exists to explain a preemption teardown.

The document therefore asks IANA to register a new protocol value, Preemption, for the Reason header, with 4 cause values. It also creates a new registry for default reason-text strings that are not SIP response codes or Q.850 causes.
sections.eli5: When someone gets cut off, the hang-up message has no good way to say 'you were bumped for something more important'. This RFC adds the missing words.

sections.title: Access Preemption Events
sections.content:
An Access Preemption Event (APE) happens at a user agent. A UA receives a new session request with an R-P value higher than the one on its active session and, under local policy, must drop the existing session to accept the new one. It does not matter whether the UA was the caller or the callee.

The preempting UA has to tell the other side why the session vanished, and BYE is the appropriate way. If the UA is the mixer in an ad hoc conference of three or more parties, a BYE must go to every UA in the conference.

The RFC lists five requirements (APE_REQ#1 to #5). They include informing the far-end UA, informing SIP elements such as proxies that used Record-Route, informing all conference participants, using an indication distinct from the network case, and allowing the indication to be generalized for the receiving UA so it cannot display more than the domain wants the user to see.

Without a dedicated value, a Reason of 410, 480, 486 or 503 would be questionable, since the session is already established.
sections.eli5: If your friend leaves your game because a teacher called them away, they should tell you it was the teacher, not that they got bored.

sections.title: Network and Hybrid Preemption
sections.content:
A Network Preemption Event (NPE) happens when a router between the UAs reaches capacity on an interface and drops one or more lower-priority reservations to admit a higher-priority one. In RSVP, a ResvErr message carries an error code explaining the teardown, but it travels downstream to the receiver and does not reach the other UA. NSIS can do the same with a NOTIFY carrying Transient error code 0x04000005 (Resources Pre-empted).

The RFC proposes that the UA that receives the reservation error send a SIP BYE, so the far-end UA and any proxies learn what happened. The R-P value in the INVITE is translated into an RSVP priority for the flow. The RFC notes that SIP itself does not start or end RSVP or NSIS signaling, which is a separate API within each UA.

A hybrid case adds a SIP gateway to a non-IP (TDM) network. If the TDM side preempts the session and tells the gateway, the gateway must convey that into SIP as if the TDM user were a UA. Requirements are NPE_REQ#1 to #4 and HYB_REQ#1 and #2.
sections.eli5: Sometimes the cutoff is made by a road along the way, not by the person you are talking to. The person at the end then tells the other side what happened.

sections.title: The Four Preemption Cause Codes
sections.content:
The new protocol value is Preemption, and its cause parameter holds a preemption cause code. Four are defined:

  • 1 UA Preemption: a UA purposely preempted the session and informs the far-end UA or UAs and stateful SIP proxies.
  • 2 Reserved Resources Preempted: a router preempted a reservation, producing a ResvErr in RSVP or a NOTIFY in NSIS. The UA that gets it sends the BYE. This is a purposeful preemption, not a link error.
  • 3 Generic Preemption: a limited-use indication for the final leg to the preempted UA.
  • 4 Non-IP Preemption: the preemption occurred in a non-IP part of the infrastructure, and the SIP gateway gives this cause.

An example is Reason: preemption ;cause=1 ;text="UA Preemption". The text is a default string, not mandatory, and may differ.
sections.eli5: There are four kinds of 'you were bumped' notes: bumped by the other phone, bumped by the network, a plain 'bumped' note, and bumped from an old-style phone line.

sections.title: Call Flows and the Generic Code
sections.content:
In the access example, UA1 calls UA2 with R-P level 3, and the session is established. UA3 then invites UA2 with R-P level 2, which is higher priority in that domain. Local policy requires UA2 to preempt, so UA2 sends UA1 a BYE with cause=1. This informs UA1 and relevant SIP elements.

In the network example, UA2 receives a ResvErr with a preemption error code from the router, then sends UA1 a BYE with cause=2. UA1 and any proxies are now synchronized.

Cause 3 is for domains that do not want the preempted UA to learn the precise type. It MUST NOT be the initial indication, because traffic analysis and network management applications would lose detail. If used, it SHOULD only be applied at the final SIP proxy, which changes the cause to 3 for the last hop.

In the non-IP example, UA1 is in a session with a user behind a gateway. When the TDM side signals preemption, the gateway sends UA1 a BYE with cause=4.
sections.eli5: The note says exactly who bumped you, unless the last helper in the chain swaps it for a simpler 'you were bumped' note to avoid showing too much.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
The existing Reason header registry lists SIP (status code) and Q.850 (cause value in decimal). RFC 4411 adds a Preemption row whose cause is a decimal value, with the reference RFC 4411.

Because Reason-text had only come from SIP response strings or Q.850 descriptions, the RFC also creates a new registry of default Reason-text strings for any protocol namespace other than those two. The strings are non-binding and meant only for human understanding, and local policy can change them. The registry starts with the four Preemption entries. Further Preemption cause codes MUST be defined in Standards Track documents.
sections.eli5: The RFC adds the four notes to an official list so everyone uses the same wording.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Eavesdropping on this header should not stop SIP from working, but some domains will want the header's integrity assured. The RFC therefore RECOMMENDS integrity protection to prevent unwanted changes to the field and snooping of the messages. The accepted choices in SIP are TLS and S/MIME.
sections.eli5: If someone could change the note, they could lie about why the call ended, so it should be sealed in an envelope.

items.label: UA Preemption
items.desc: The session has been preempted by a UA.

items.label: Reserved Resources Preempted
items.desc: Preemption initiated within the network through a purposeful RSVP preemption, not a link error.

items.label: Generic Preemption
items.desc: Limited-use indication for the final leg to the preempted UA.

items.label: Non-IP Preemption
items.desc: Preemption in a non-IP part of the infrastructure, reported by the SIP gateway.
